newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC COACH BRIAN HILL FIRED; ADUBATO TAKES OVER.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MAGIC COACH BRIAN HILL FIRED; ADUBATO TAKES OVER.

text.p: Less than two years after he guided the team to the NBA Finals, Brian Hill was fired as head coach of the Orlando Magic.
The team announced Tuesday that Hill had been replaced by assistant coach Richie Adubato, who will serve as interim coach for the remainder of the season.

Hill had never won less than 50 games in any of his three full seasons with the Magic. But the team suffered its fifth consecutive loss Monday to drop to 24-25 amid growing reports of a rift between Hill and some of his players and questions about his ability to movitate the team.
"All I know is there was a request to make a change," Hill said. "I'm not bitter with any of the players. I have a lot of respect for the guys who've played here the last 3 1/2 years."
After inheriting a team in 1993 which featured young superstars Shaquille O'Neal and Penny Hardaway, Hill posted a 191-104 mark in 3 1/2 seasons as coach, including a trip to the Finals in 1995.

But Hill suffered the defection of O'Neal, who signed a huge free agent contract with the Los Angeles Lakers during the offseason, and extended injuries to three starters, including Hardaway, who missed 23 games.

When Hardaway, Nick Anderson and Dennis Scott returned from their injuries in mid-January, the Magic caught fire, winning 13 of 16 games prior to the All-Star break. But Orlando has not won since, appearing lethargic in its five losses.
"We were on a pretty good roll before the All-Star Game," said Adubato. "Now we're going to have to sit down as a group and decide how we can get back on track."
Adubato, 59, has been with the Magic since 1994. He served as coach of the Detroit Pistons in 1979-80 and the Dallas Mavericks from 1989 to 1993, posting a career mark of 106-228.
"It's a very difficult day for me, due to the fact that I've had a great relationship with Brian Hill way back to his high school days when he was a player for me," Adubato said.
"We were very close. We have been friends for many, many years," added Adubato, the third coach in the eight-year history of the Magic.
